name: kvd
algorithm: Run the kvd dogfood's crash-and-recovery simulation over a range of seeds under std.sim: per seed, a server and three clients of 16 steps on a simulated disk and network, crashed at a log write, faulted or shut down, recovered from its log and checked, then the summary of every run (README.md).
notes: Tier A (M9 item 11.32): an Mk-only row, the kvd dogfood unchanged, compared across mk binaries; no twin, no peer, no defect line (README.md).
kvd declares one unsafe module, src/snap (its snapshot recovery through fs.Map), which keeps it out of a twinned bench.json row unchanged (D-781); an Mk-only row may keep it, labelled.

The mode is sim, not the bench case the programme named: kvd bench syncs its log on every write (SyncPolicy.Always, fixed in src/main/bench.mk), so every write waits for a sync, and it needs a fresh data directory per run, which an output file does not give (README.md, Why sim).
The size (the seed range) is provisional; tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes it in the quiet window, and the checksum changes with it.
